body_markdown:
# Margaret Telfer (1801–?)

**Role:** Sister of Francis Telfer (1809–1895), stayed in Scotland

Margaret Telfer was born ~1801 at Greenholm, near Newcastleton, Roxburghshire, Scotland. She was the fourth child of James Telfer (1761–1845), a hand loom weaver, and Elizabeth "Betty" Hutton (1774–1853).

She did NOT emigrate to Australia and stayed in Scotland.

The book *From the Borders to the Bush* states: *"We have no further information about four members of this family; namely Isobel, Adam, Margaret and William."* Like her siblings Isobel, Adam, and William, Margaret's fate after the family records is not documented.

**Source:** *From the Borders to the Bush* — pages 17–20

---

## Family Stories

### Stayed Behind

Margaret Telfer was born around 1801 at Greenholm — the fourth child of James Telfer and Elizabeth Hutton. While her brothers Francis and John crossed the ocean to South Australia, Margaret stayed in Scotland. She never emigrated and remained in Scotland.

Like her siblings Isobel, Adam, and William, the book *From the Borders to the Bush* has no further record of her life. While a new branch of the family took root on the other side of the world, Margaret remained in the valley she was born in — part of the old world that the emigrants left behind, though her later years are unrecorded.

*(From the Borders to the Bush, pp.17-20)*

## Life Summary

James Telfer was the twin brother of Janet Welsh Telfer (1858–1921) — the pair shared the birth date **29 August 1858** at Tungkillo, South Australia, children of pioneer James Telfer (1829–1913) and Janet Welsh. On **14 March 1882** he married **Frances Margaret Oswald** at Port Lincoln, South Australia. Unlike his sister's line (which carried no children through her marriage to Andrew Watherstone), James's line carried deep through the Fraser/Donnelly families via his daughters. He died **27 July 1944** at Medindie Gardens, South Australia, aged 85, and was buried at the North Road Cemetery, Nailsworth, alongside his wife on a shared family headstone.

> **⚠️ Do not conflate:** This James Telfer (1858–1944) is the *son and twin*. He must not be confused with his father **James Telfer (1829–1913)** of Koppio, nor with the unrelated James Telford / other James Telfers elsewhere in the tree. The shared 29 Aug 1858 twin birth date is his signature identifier.

Herbert Clifford Holloway was born **16 September 1887** near **Tantanoola**, South Australia, the son of **Thomas Holloway** (Port Adelaide-born) and **Elizabeth Telfer (Farrow) Holloway**, daughter of Charles Farrow and Elizabeth Hannah Telfer of Hope Farm, Tarlee. His place of association in the service records is **Tantanoola, South Australia**.

### Military Service (World War I)

Herbert enlisted in the Australian Imperial Force in World War I and served as a **Trooper in the 9th Australian Light Horse Regiment** (Service No. 1554) — the mounted infantry of the Australian Light Horse.

Trooper Herbert Clifford Holloway died on **3 December 1918** in **Egypt**, of **illness (pneumonia)** — days after the Armistice that ended the fighting, a wartime casualty who did not make it home to the South-East. He was buried at **Cairo War Memorial Cemetery, Egypt**, and is commemorated at panel **7** in the Commemorative Area at the **Australian War Memorial, Canberra**.

# William Francis "Frank" Telfer (1885–1955)

**Role:** Elder son of George Wright Telfer and Ruth Penna — Merredin storekeeper, Road Board chairman, and MLA for Avon (1943–47). The son who carried the family westward branch into Western Australia's Wheatbelt.

**Born:** 21 August 1885 — Gawler, South Australia
**Died:** 25 August 1955 (aged 70) — Subiaco, Western Australia
**Buried:** Merredin Cemetery, Western Australia
**Occupation:** Storekeeper, farmer, politician (MLA Avon 1943–47), Merredin Road Board member & chairman
**Spouse:** Ethel May Wisher (m. 17 March 1913, Lake St Chapel, Perth)

## Family

| Relation | Name |
|----------|------|
| **Father** | [[George Wright Telfer (1850–1913)]] |
| **Mother** | Ruth Penna (1863–1908) |
| **Spouse** | Ethel May Wisher (m. 17 Mar 1913, d. 1944) |
| **Children** | Three sons and one daughter |

**Siblings:** Olive Millie Telfer (1890–1890), Lesley Thomas Telfer (1892–1914), Olive Netta Telfer Thomas (1894–1986)

## Life Summary

William Francis "Frank" Telfer was born on **21 August 1885** at Gawler, South Australia, the eldest son of **George Wright Telfer** and **Ruth (Penna) Telfer**. He grew up at Kersbrook and Willaston before his father moved the whole family west to Western Australia. Frank came to the eastern Wheatbelt with his father around **1910**, settling in **Merredin**, where he opened the Telfer store and agency and took up wheat farming.

He served the Merredin community for decades: **Merredin Road Board 1936–1955, chairman from 1938**, member of the executive of the Road Board Association 1943–1950, and Secretary of the Merredin Agricultural Society for many years.

### Political Career

Frank was elected to the **Western Australian Legislative Assembly** as the **Labor member for Avon** at the **1943 state election**, defeating the sitting Country member Ignatius Boyle by 15 votes. That result was overturned in the Court of Disputed Returns, but Frank again defeated Boyle at the resulting by-election in **1944**. At the **1947 election**, as the Labor government fell, he lost the seat to Country candidate George Cornell. He retired from the road board after 1947.

Frank died at **St John of God Hospital, Subiaco**, on **25 August 1955**, aged 70, and was buried at **Merredin Cemetery**. *(Note: the family book *From the Borders to the Bush* gives his death as 1956; the verified record is 1955 — Wikipedia and the WA Parliament register agree on 25 Aug 1955.)*

## Family Stories

### Frank the Politician *(as told in From the Borders to the Bush, p.183)*

Frank served on the Merredin Road Board from 1936 to 1955 (chairman 1938–55) and was MLA for Avon from 1943 to 1947. He was instrumental in local development of the Merredin district — the storekeeper who rose to represent the Wheatbelt in parliament.

> **🖊️ Anecdote — as told in *From the Borders to the Bush* (p.183)** — the portrait of Frank in his Merredin political prime: from the family store and wheat paddocks to the floor of the Western Australian parliament.

## Timeline

|------|-------|

| c. 1896 | Family moves to Western Australia with father George |
| 1910 | Arrives in the eastern Wheatbelt (Merredin) with his father |
| 17 Mar 1913 | Married Ethel May Wisher, Lake St Chapel, Perth (Church of Christ) |
| 1936 | Elected to Merredin Road Board |
| 1938 | Becomes Road Board chairman |
| 15 Aug 1944 | Wife Ethel died (Widowed) |
| 1943–1947 | MLA for Avon (Labor), contested/held seat 1943–47 |
| 1947 | Lost seat; retired from active politics |
| 25 Aug 1955 | Died, Subiaco, Western Australia; buried Merredin Cemetery |

Ethel May Wisher 17 Mar 1913; widowed 15 Aug 1944; three sons & one daughter; d. 25 Aug 1955, buried Merredin Cemetery; Road Board 1936–1955 chairman 1938 — accessed 31 August 2026

# Kenneth William John Telfer

**Role:** Second child and eldest son of Mark Telfer and Julia Seebohm

## Gravestone

*Image to be added — headstone photo of Ken's grave at Tantanoola Cemetery is yet to be sourced. [View the headstone transcription and cemetery records](http://www.ozburials.com/CemsSA/tantanoola.htm)*

Kenneth William John Telfer (the family book *From the Borders to the Bush* records his middle names as William John, not Alexander) was the second child and eldest son of Mark Telfer (1877–1946) and Julia Matilda Seebohm (1876–1939) of Tantanoola, South Australia. He was born **27 August 1906** at Tantanoola and died on **9 November 1970**, aged 64, and is buried at Tantanoola Cemetery.

## Verified facts

- **Name:** Kenneth William John Telfer — confirmed by the South Australian birth, marriage and death registrations (below), the Tantanoola Cemetery headstone transcription (Ozburials: "TELFER, Kenneth William John. 9 November 1970. Aged 64"), FamilySearch (1906–1970), and *From the Borders to the Bush* p.243.
- **Birth:** **27 August 1906**, Tantanoola — SA Birth Reg **Book 771/Page 420** (Genealogy SA). Father Mark TELFER, mother Julia Matilda SEEBOHM. The family book's "1904" was an error; age 64 at death and age 32 at first marriage both accord with a 1906 birth.
- **Parents:** Mark Telfer (1877–1946) and Julia Matilda Seebohm (1876–1939). Confirmed on his SA birth and marriage registrations.
- **First marriage:** **Jessie Kathleen SARGENT** — **4 February 1939**, Presbyterian Church, Millicent — SA Marriage Reg **Book 396/Page 456** (Genealogy SA). Groom K.W.J. TELFER, 32, single, son of Mark TELFER; bride Jessie Kathleen SARGENT, 24, single. Jessie died 26 June 1954 and is buried beside him at Tantanoola.
- **Second marriage:** **Gwendoline Victoria CAMPBELL** — his second wife. Confirmed by her SA Death Reg **Book 17A/6787**: Gwendoline Victoria TELFER, died 18 September 1966, Millicent, married, relative Kenneth William John TELFER. Her death registration precedes Kenneth's as widower.
- **Death:** **9 November 1970**, aged 64, widower, Millicent — SA Death Reg **Book 106A/Page 8861** (Genealogy SA); relative "Gwendoline Victoria TELFER (deceased wife)" [DW]. Also shown on headstone transcription + FamilySearch.

## Family record

The following is family knowledge / word of mouth, as recorded in the family history book — shared as the family record, not yet independently verified against public records.

Ken and his first wife Jessie had a son, **Murray**, who married Susanne Maloney and had five children — Joanne, Mark (who married Maryann Harrap), John, Richard and Neville. Jessie died in 1954. Kenneth later remarried (Gwendoline Victoria Campbell); no children of the second marriage are recorded.

## Stories from the family

These come from word of mouth / family history passed down *(From the Borders to the Bush, p.243)*:

Ken played football for Tantanoola for many years. He was Captain of the team and played at centre. He also played in the Tantanoola cricket team, being a useful bat and a slow bowler. In later years he played bowls, both indoor and outdoor. He held the position of President of the Tantanoola Pastoral, Agricultural and Horticultural Society from 1953 to 1955.

- Tantanoola Cemetery headstone transcription — [Ozburials.com](http://www.ozburials.com/CemsSA/tantanoola.htm)

# Reginald Masters Telfer (1922–2011)

## Official Records — SA registrations (verified 3 Sep 2026, Genealogy SA)

**Birth:** TELFER, Reginald Masters — born **11 Dec 1922**, Tumby Bay, Flinders district; father **Francis Charles TELFER**, mother **Amy Ellen PROVIS**. *(SA Birth Registration Book 107A/Page 542)*

**Marriage:** TELFER, Reginald Masters ↔ **PUGSLEY, Elma Ellen Martina** — married **27 Mar 1945**, Flinders district; groom father Francis Charles TELFER; bride father **Frederick Arthur PUGSLEY**. *(SA Marriage Registration Book 479/Page 1343)*

> ⚠️ **Spelling correction (verified):** The family history renders the wife's maiden name **"Pubsley"**; the official SA marriage registration records it as **"Pugsley"** — Elma Ellen Martina **Pugsley**.

**Death:** died **30 Jul 2011** aged 88 (death notice printed Adelaide papers **2 Aug 2011**; funeral notice **5 Aug 2011**). *(Genealogy SA Newspaper Death Notices; SA official death register post-1996 not in the online index — death confirmed via newspaper notice.)*

---

## Family of Origin

Reginald Masters was the **eighth child** (born 11 Dec 1922) of Francis Charles "Charlie" Telfer and Amy Ellen Provis of the Tumby Bay / Ungarra (Eyre Peninsula) district. His younger brother Murray John Telfer (1924–2009) was Mark Telfer's paternal grandfather — so Reginald was **Mark's great-uncle**.

The sibling-cluster is consistent: elder brother Edwin Roy born 25-Aug-1919 Tumby Bay (Book 44A/51) and sister Clarice May born 22-May-1911 (Book 865/209), all children of the same parents, all Tumby Bay / Flinders — confirming the family was settled at Old Scrub Farm, Ungarra by the 1910s–20s.

---

## Marriage & Descendants

Reg married **Elma Ellen Martina Pugsley** (b. 30 Apr 1923, Lipson SA; d. 18 Feb 1996, Adelaide SA) on **27 Mar 1945** (daughter of Frederick Arthur Pugsley). They raised their family at Ungarra, SA:

- **Vonda Joy** (b. 6 Jun 1948, Tumby Bay) – m. David Grant Kelly (3 Mar 1973, Ungarra)
- **Brenda Janice** (b. 5 Oct 1949, Tumby Bay) – m. Peter James Manuel (8 May 1971, Ungarra)
- **Lyndell Marie** (b. 4 Jan 1951, Tumby Bay) – m. Robert Norman Maddern (2 Feb 1971, Ungarra)
- **Malvern Reginald** (b. 24 Apr 1953, Tumby Bay) – m. Lynette Ruth Gordge (15 Feb 1975), father of **Samuel Joel "Sam" Telfer MP**
- **David Lyndon** (b. 25 Mar 1957, Tumby Bay; d. 28 Jan 1996) – m. Kathleen Meredith Hancock (21 May 1977, Magill)

*Reg's descendants include **Samuel Joel "Sam" Telfer MP** (b. 12 Sep 1985, Tumby Bay), Liberal MP for Flinders since 2022 — Reg's grandson via Malvern Reginald. (Sam confirmed family in the 28 Aug 2026 phone call from Timothy Neil Telfer: "Uncle Reg → Malvern → Sam.")*

---

## The Old Scrub Farm, Ungarra

Reg owned and worked the **"Old Scrub Farm"** at Ungarra, SA — noted in *Some Childhood Memories* by his sister Jean McMurtrie, and in *From the Borders to the Bush* the family history records that Reg "still owned and worked 'the Old Scrub Farm' into the late 1980s — the original family property that had 'produced many good crops over the last 80 years.'" As a boy he was known for cutting his younger brother Murray's finger with scissors when Murray held it out and said "cut it." In later years he suffered from severe arthritis.

---

## Life Summary

Lesley Thomas Telfer was the third child of George Wright Telfer and Ruth Penna, born at Gawler East, South Australia in September 1891. He was a younger sibling of Frank (William Francis) and elder brother of Olive Netta. After his mother Ruth died in 1908 and the family moved west, he joined his father's farming operation in Western Australia.

Lesley was killed in an accident on 11 March 1914 while working his father's farm at Knungagen in the Nungarin district — in the same year his father George had died. He was in his early twenties. A coroner's inquest (the "Knungagen Tragedy") was held at Merredin on 18 March 1914.

## Timeline

| Date | Event |
|------|-------|
| 24 Sep 1891 | Born at Gawler East, SA ⚠️ (book single-source) |
| 1896 | Family moved to Western Australia |
| 1908 | Mother Ruth Penna died |
| 1913 | Father George Wright Telfer died |
| 11 Mar 1914 | Died in an accident at Knungagen farm, near Nungarin WA — aged ~22 |

## Sources

- **Source (death, 2-group):** [Merredin Mercury, 25 Mar 1914 — "The Knungagen Tragedy" (coroner's inquest)](https://trove.nla.gov.au/newspaper/article/155996677) — via Trove — accessed 4 Sep 2026. Confirms death morning of 11th; G. W. Telfer & Co. farm at Knungagen; deceased ~15 months on the farm.
- **Source:** *A Telfer Family Tree* (Supplement to *From the Borders to the Bush*), pp. 160 & 164 — birth 24 Sep 1891 Gawler East (single-source); death 11 Mar 1914 Talgomine/Nungarin WA accident.

## Family Stories

🖊️ **Anecdote — the "Knungagen Tragedy" (as told in *A Telfer Family Tree*, pp.163–164 + Merredin Mercury inquest):** Lesley, third child of George Wright and Ruth, was single and working his father's farm at Knungagen in the Nungarin district when he died on the morning of 11 March 1914 aged about 22. A farm labourer told the inquest Lesley had been on the farm about 15 months, had ridden to Merredin on the 9th and returned about midnight on the 10th before his sudden death. He died in the same year his father George had passed, years before his sister Olive Netta and brother Frank carried the family on. *(Anecdote — not used to establish any date or relationship beyond the verified death.)*
